results.title: Arc FIFO yields complete four-page batches repeatedly to a late third pane under backlog
Arc removes hidden or closed FIFO waiters without retaining a reserved lease

findings: Controlled-response hidden and queued-dispose case actually passed in this run.
Backlog case failed at line65: some peer had not begun its second batch when another began its third. Raw failure only records boolean false, not task/cursor/request order.
First run passed backlog and failed removal; second passed removal and failed backlog. These cannot be combined into a whole-suite PASS.
staticDiagnosis: Polling for >=2 patch requests does not freeze when the late third pane joins.

The strict global batch-round predicate can exceed work-conserving FIFO semantics: a still-inflight slow peer is not yet a waiter, so another free slot may continue serving actual queued work. Without saved trace this is a hypothesis, not the actual unique cause.

Next bounded source observation should retain real request order/late-join cursors and control actual response boundaries. Verify waiting participants receive released leases before a holder reacquires, complete bounded batches, repeated progress, two-lease peak and hidden/closed cleanup. Any corrected acceptance semantics must be explained and reviewed; preserve old FAIL evidence.
limits: No product regression root cause established and no product correctness claim.
Exact recorded PID/PGID7418 ESRCH and own scratch absent. Regular-file logs are not dual pipe EOF, and no independent port probe was performed.
Root only read files/source; no additional test, process probe, browser or HTTP scenario.
Owner continues manager-assigned ordinary diagnosis; no automatic retry or transfer of old runtime. Personal restoration has priority.
